product_overview: A Flask-backed web application that reorders sentences using baseline and parsing models and records run history, planned to evolve into a fully immersive 3D WebGL visualization of dependency parses. The frontend interacts with existing APIs (reorder, sample, history) and supports Google-based authentication for optional saved runs.
core_goals: Provide accurate sentence reordering using baseline and parser approaches via POST /api/reorder
Expose an intuitive user flow for entering text, running reordering, and inspecting results (table/cards) on /reorder
Enable optional Google-based authentication to persist runs and present user-aware state without gating core functionality
Maintain run history management (view, add, delete, clear) via /history and associated APIs
Support sample input loading from the Reuters dataset via GET /api/sample and present graceful error handling
Prepare the frontend contract and data mappings required to evolve the UI into a 3D WebGL/R3F experience while keeping REST API compatibility

features.name: User Authentication
features.description: Allow users to authenticate using Google (Firebase) so they can optionally save runs and see an authenticated state; authentication is optional and not required to use core reordering functionality.
user_flows: Navigate to /login -> Initiate Google sign-in -> Complete Google authentication -> Receive auth status from /api/auth/status -> See authenticated state on /
Navigate to /login -> Initiate Google sign-in -> User cancels or provider rejects authentication -> Receive error from /api/auth/google -> See authentication error message on /login
Navigate to / -> Initiate logout -> Send POST to /api/auth/logout -> See unauthenticated state on /

features.name: Sentence Reordering
features.description: Accept user text input, run baseline and/or parsing reordering models via POST /api/reorder, and present results as comparative table and cards; allow loading example text from GET /api/sample.
user_flows: Navigate to /reorder -> Enter text for reordering -> Request parser reordering via POST /api/reorder -> Receive parser results -> See reordering results displayed as table and cards on /reorder
Navigate to /reorder -> Enter text for reordering -> Request baseline reordering via POST /api/reorder -> Receive baseline results -> See baseline results displayed as table and cards on /reorder

Navigate to /reorder -> Load example from dataset via GET /api/sample -> See example text populated into input -> Request compare reordering via POST /api/reorder -> Receive both baseline and parser payloads -> See side-by-side comparison of outputs on /reorder
Navigate to /reorder -> Submit empty or invalid text -> Receive validation error from /api/reorder -> See input validation error on /reorder
Navigate to /reorder -> Enter text for reordering -> Request reordering -> Server returns processing error or times out -> See processing error message on /reorder

features.name: Run History
features.description: Display recent runs, allow users to add runs to history, delete individual items, and clear the full history via /history backed by GET/POST/DELETE history APIs.
user_flows: Navigate to /history -> Retrieve run list from /api/history -> See run history table populated on /history
Navigate to /reorder -> Complete a successful reordering -> Send run data to /api/history -> See new run entry appear when viewing /history
Navigate to /history -> Delete a specific run -> Send DELETE to /api/history/<id> -> See run removed from history on /history
Navigate to /history -> Clear history -> Send DELETE to /api/history -> See empty history state on /history
Navigate to /history -> Attempt to delete a run -> Server returns failure from DELETE /api/history/<id> -> See deletion error message on /history
Navigate to /history -> Attempt to clear history -> Server returns failure from DELETE /api/history -> See clear-history error message on /history
